CPM Group 's Jeffrey Christian laid out a precious metals outlook in which firmer gold and silver prices would not hinge on a U.S. dollar collapse, the research firm said. The presentation also covered silver trading under the $60 level and the forces behind investment demand at historically elevated levels.
Gold changed hands near $4,160 and stayed mostly inside its recent $4,050 to $4,200 band. Christian observed that the longer the metal goes without a decisive push higher, the greater the chance of an initial slide toward $4,000 or lower over the coming days or weeks. Even with that near-term risk, CPM Group anticipates that investors will add to gold purchases and underpin higher prices over the next several months, with that strength potentially carrying into 2028.
Silver traded near $58.25 at the time of recording and kept showing more weakness than gold. Christian discussed how prices could decline further as the U.S. congressional elections draw closer, and CPM Group sees significant political and economic risks lifting prices after the vote. The presentation also reviewed platinum near $1,661 and palladium near $1,119, after palladium's earlier fall below $1,100.
Christian presented data showing the dollar's strength alongside gains in central bank and international investor holdings of dollars and U.S. Treasuries. He drew a distinction between diversifying a portfolio and cutting total dollar holdings, and explained why a firmer dollar does not automatically translate into lower gold and silver prices. CPM Group also noted that investors frequently purchase gold, silver, dollars and U.S. Treasuries simultaneously when economic and political risks are high or increasing.
CPM Group describes itself as a commodities research, consulting, financial advisory and commodities management firm that provides independent research and analysis on commodities markets, corporate and project finance, and exposure management for commodity-oriented investments. The firm said it began operations in 1986 with the aim of delivering commodities research and advice through independent experts without ties to banks, brokers, mining companies or other entities whose interests could conflict with clients.
